params.body:
**Shane, 20 September 2026: a bidding runs up to and including its end date.** So the offer and the
heading were right and the countdown was wrong — and that one answer settles two findings.

**#570 was already half fixed.** The bid form stopped disagreeing on 15 September: it reads the same
`ExportVehicle::isBiddingOpen` as the label, so the last day counts there too. The finding was stale
and nobody had gone back to it.

**#576 was not.** The older POST route the list uses to place a bid checked the reserve price and the
bidder's own highest bid, and nothing else. A bid that arrived days after the bidding closed was
accepted and could become the highest — quietly, with a notification to the selling dealer as if
everything were normal. It reads the same helper now and sends the bidder back with the reason.

Two rules leave the disputed state and say what was decided:

| | |
|---|---|
| R B1-3.1 | runs through the end date; every screen and every road to a bid reads one helper |
| R B1-4.4 | a closed bidding accepts no bid at all, however high |

Three tests: the end date itself, the day after, and a bidding with no end date (which stays open).
Checked by taking the guard out again — the middle one fails.

**And one observation from going through your list.** Of the 26 findings marked "beslist: shane"
with severity *nu* or *deze week*, about three are actually questions. The rest are plain defects
with an obvious right answer — a typo (`rol_id` for `role_id`) that makes a rights cascade do
nothing, `DELETE vehicle/{id}` answering "successfully deleted" while deleting nothing since
February, Dutch postcodes refused while we serve Dutch dealers, a rental pdf readable by any signed
in user. Those do not need your answer, they need doing. The label was put on everything that was
not clearly Ilse's when the findings were mirrored; it does not mean they are all decisions.
